questions.q: ___ is known as the father of modern psychology.
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Wundt is called the father of modern (experimental) psychology because he founded the first psychology laboratory in Leipzig in 1879. Freud founded psychoanalysis and Watson founded behaviorism.

questions.q: Cognitivists objected to behaviorists because they felt that behaviorists ignored the important role of ___.
questions.explanation: Cognitivists argued that behaviorists ignored internal mental processes such as thinking, memory and problem solving, focusing only on observable stimulus-response links.

questions.q: ___ is viewed as the mainstream for all research on learning designs.
questions.explanation: Cognitivism, with its focus on how information is processed, stored and retrieved, became the mainstream framework for research on learning and instructional design after the cognitive revolution.

questions.q: ___ is a perspective in psychology focusing on the belief that human consciousness cannot be broken down into its elements and is based on the concept of a 'whole'.
questions.explanation: Gestalt psychology holds that the whole is different from the sum of its parts, so experience and consciousness should be studied as organized wholes rather than broken into elements.

questions.q: Theory of multiple intelligences is given by
questions.explanation: Howard Gardner proposed the theory of multiple intelligences in 1983 (Frames of Mind). Sternberg proposed the triarchic theory, and Tolman is known for cognitive maps.

questions.q: The general intelligence factor, also known as g, is what intelligence tests typically measure and refers only to ___ intelligence.
questions.explanation: Critics such as Sternberg and Gardner argue that g, as measured by standard IQ tests, captures only academic (analytical) intelligence and misses practical, creative and other abilities.

questions.q: Cognitive evaluation for planning, attention, simultaneous, and successive processing of individuals can be done through CAS based on PASS theory. CAS here stands for ___.
questions.explanation: The Cognitive Assessment System (Das and Naglieri) operationalizes PASS theory by measuring Planning, Attention, Simultaneous and Successive processing.

questions.q: BBL is a new science that shapes the learning process and is an approach that is based on the structure and function of the human brain. BBL stands for ___.
questions.explanation: BBL stands for brain-based learning, an approach that designs teaching around how the brain naturally learns, using findings from neuroscience.

questions.q: Gagne's Conditions of Learning is also known as ___ Events of Instruction.
questions.explanation: Gagne's Conditions of Learning gives nine events of instruction, from gaining attention to enhancing retention and transfer.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a type of constructivism?
questions.explanation: Common types of constructivism are cognitive (Piaget), social (Vygotsky) and radical (von Glasersfeld). Biological constructivism is not one of the recognized types.
